title: Machine-learning classification dates a tectonic transition and probable slab detachment in central Tibet
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set. Applied to basalts from Tibet’s Bangong–Nujiang suture zone, it found mixed signatures before about 108–107 Ma and only destructive-boundary signatures afterward; the authors interpret the transition as likely oceanic-slab detachment, consistent with other geological evidence.
ai_technology: Random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element concentrations
organization: China Geological Survey; Chengdu University of Technology; University of Canterbury; China University of Mining and Technology; Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory; Hunan University of Science and Technology; Nanjing University; China University of Geosciences (Beijing); Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: A random-forest classifier trained on global basalt trace-element data distinguished destructive from constructive plate-boundary signatures, with the paper reporting greater than 98% accuracy on its labeled evaluation set.
evidence.unknown: The specific age and slab-detachment interpretation are geological inferences from classified basalt geochemistry, not direct observation of a detached slab. The authors describe the detachment explanation as likely and note consistency with existing evidence; model accuracy is not independent confirmation of the tectonic interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The classifier learned trace-element signatures associated with destructive and constructive plate boundaries and applied them to Tibetan suture-zone basalts, revealing a time-ordered change in inferred tectonic setting that supported the authors’ slab-detachment interpretation.
